questions.question: Which of the following is NOT related to reticulate venation?
questions.solution:
Maize is not related to reticulate venation; it possesses parallel venation.
  • Riculate venation is a characteristic of dicot plants (like Coriander, China rose, and Tulsi) where veins form a net-like network.
  • In monocots like Maize, Grass, and Wheat, the veins run parallel to each other from the base to the tip of the leaf.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of Phylum Arthropoda?
questions.solution:
The Butterfly is a classic example of the Phylum Arthropoda.
  • Arthropoda is the largest phylum in the animal kingdom, characterized by jointed appendages and a chitinous exoskeleton.
  • Note: Nereis and Hirudinaria (leech) belong to Annelida, while Pila (apple snail) belongs to Mollusca.

questions.question: In the year 1925, who extracted lipids from an erythrocyte sample and found that lipid monolayers are good for measuring molecular surface area versus lateral pressure?
questions.solution:
In 1925, Gorter and Grendel performed the landmark experiment of extracting lipids from erythrocytes (red blood cells).
  • By spreading these lipids as a monolayer, they discovered the surface area was exactly twice the area of the cells, leading to the conclusion that the cell membrane is a lipid bilayer.
  • This was a fundamental step toward the modern understanding of the fluid mosaic model of cell membranes.

questions.question: Which law states that endothermic animals from cold climates have smaller extremities or appendages than closely related species from warm climates?
questions.solution:
Allen’s rule states that endothermic (warm-blooded) animals in colder climates have shorter limbs, ears, and appendages compared to those in warmer regions.
  • This adaptation helps minimize heat loss by reducing the total surface area exposed to the cold environment.
  • For example, the Arctic Fox has much smaller ears and a shorter muzzle than the Fennec Fox found in the Sahara Desert.
